      Introduction

       The NITI Aayog has released the second annual edition of the “Fiscal Health Index (FHI)
       2026” to assess and compare the fiscal performance of Indian states. This edition of the
        FHI evaluates fiscal performance for FY 2023–24 and expands coverage to include North-
        Eastern and Himalayan states, making the analysis more comprehensive.


     Background: About Fiscal Health Index

           FHI provides a comprehensive and comparable assessment of the fiscal performance
            of Indian states.

                    It is designed as a data-driven framework to evaluate fiscal soundness, guide reforms,
          and promote evidence-based fiscal policymaking.

                    It evaluates fiscal soundness, encourages reforms, and supports evidence-based fiscal
            policymaking.



      Need for the Fiscal Health Index

             Globally, public finances are under increasing pressure, making sound fiscal
          management essential for macroeconomic stability and long-term development.





Fiscal Health Index 2026                                                                                                                 1

In India:

                State governments account for nearly one-third of general government debt.

                States have significant responsibilities for public service delivery and development
                expenditure.

            Therefore, systematic monitoring of state finances is crucial to ensure fiscal discipline,
              efficient resource allocation, and sustainable public finances.

             Fiscal Health Index helps by:

               Enabling benchmarking across states

                 Identifying areas requiring fiscal reforms.


      Highlights of FHI 2026



          Expanded Coverage: FHI 2026 expands the scope of the framework.

             The first edition of FHI assessed the fiscal performance of 18 major states,

             The second edition of FHI 2026 includes the 10 North-Eastern and Himalayan
                 states, making the FHI more inclusive and representative of India’s fiscal diversity.

           Separate Evaluation: Due to structural differences, North-Eastern and Himalayan states
            are ranked separately from the major states.

           Methodology/Fiscal Parameters:

              Data used to calculate the FHI (major variables & sub-components under each
                 variable) is sourced from the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG).

              Comprehensive overview of budgetary transactions for all states for the period
             2023-24 is utilised for FHI 2026 calculation and subsequent analysis.

             Fiscal indicators for North-Eastern and Himalayan states were refined to reflect their
           unique characteristics, such as:

                   Difficult terrain and remoteness

              Sparse population density

                Limited own revenue capacity

               Higher service delivery costs

               Greater dependence on Union government transfers.

            Categorisation: States are ranked based on their computed FHI scores, with the
           topperforming state receiving the first rank. Further they are classified in four
            categories based on their FHI score viz

              Major States

                  Performer

      Fiscal Performance of States

        According to FHI 2026, fiscal outcomes across Indian states show significant variation in
          fiscal discipline, debt sustainability, and revenue performance. The analysis evaluates fiscal
        trends for 2023–24 compared to 2022–23, highlighting differences in fiscal management
      among states.



       Performance of 18 Major States

      Among the 18 major states, fiscal performance differs based on debt levels, fiscal deficits,
       and revenue mobilisation.

           Leading State: Odisha continues to top the FHI due to:

                Controlled fiscal deficits

                Stable revenue mobilisation.

           States Improving in Ranking: Jharkhand and Gujarat

              Both states recorded slight improvements in ranking, supported by stable debt and
              revenue flows despite minor declines in scores.

           States Showing Decline in Fiscal Indicators: Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan

             These states slipped in ranking due to weakening fiscal indicators.

           States with Stable Fiscal Performance: Maharashtra and Telangana

              Both states remained broadly stable in fiscal performance.

           States with Mixed Fiscal Outcomes: Bihar and Madhya Pradesh





Fiscal Health Index 2026                                                                                                                 7

Their fiscal position is constrained by high committed expenditure, including
                  salaries, pensions, and interest payments.

           States Facing Persistent Fiscal Stress: Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, Kerala.
          These states face continued fiscal pressure due to:

                Rising debt levels

                Persistent fiscal deficits

            Weak revenue growth.



       Performance of North-Eastern and Himalayan States

       The North-Eastern and Himalayan states show wide variation in fiscal performance due to
         structural and geographic differences.

           Leading State: Arunachal Pradesh leads due to:

               Strong expenditure quality

               Prudent debt management.

           Strong Revenue Performance: Uttarakhand performs well due to high own-revenue
             mobilisation.

           Strong Debt Sustainability: Tripura shows strong performance in debt sustainability
             indicators.

           States with Mixed Fiscal Outcomes: Meghalaya and Assam

                Their performance reflects varying strengths in revenue mobilisation, expenditure
                  quality, and fiscal discipline.

           States Facing Structural Constraints: Himachal Pradesh and Manipur

             These states face challenges such as high committed expenditure and weak
              revenue mobilisation capacity.




         Highlights: Major States

          Odisha remains the top performer, improving its score over the previous year, with Goa
          and Jharkhand also featuring among the top Achiever states.

            Gujarat and Maharashtra continue in the top five, while Haryana records a notable year-
           on-year improvement of three ranks.





Fiscal Health Index 2026                                                                                                                 8

Bihar, Karnataka and Telangana show a mild recovery, whereas Punjab, West Bengal
          and Kerala remain at the bottom of the rankings.

             Overall, higher-ranked states display stronger fiscal discipline and resource mobilisation
              efforts, while lower ranked states exhibit higher non-developmental expenditure and
             less sustainable fiscal patterns.

           Achiever group (Odisha, Goa and Jharkhand) is characterised by high own- tax shares
           (above 60%), relatively large capital outlay (around 4-5% of GSDP), low fiscal deficits
           (below 3% of GSDP), moderate debt levels (under 25% of GSDP) and contained interest
           burdens.

           Front-Runner states (Gujarat, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh and
            Karnataka) and Performer states (Madhya Pradesh, Haryana, Bihar, Tamil Nadu and
            Rajasthan) broadly maintain their positions with minor reshuffling, though their scores
           moderate slightly compared to the previous year.

            Aspirational states (West Bengal, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Punjab) face persistent

             Revenue and fiscal deficits often breaching FRBM norms

               Elevated debt levels of roughly 35-45% of GSDP

              Committed expenditure accounting for about 50-60% of revenue receipts

              Large interest payments exceeding 15-20%

                 Relatively low developmental spending.

          Most states strengthened on Quality of Expenditure

              Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh moving from Front Runner to Achiever

                 Gujarat, Rajasthan, Andhra Pradesh improving from Performer to Front Runner.

            Majority of states, retained their earlier category.

         Goa and Odisha continue to record high State Own Revenue ratios, reflecting strong tax
           bases and greater fiscal autonomy.

           Jharkhand slipped from Front Runner to Performer, while most other states witnessed
            only marginal reshuffling within the same category.

            Bihar improved from Aspirational to Performer, signalling better deficit management.

              In contrast, Karnataka and Telangana moved from Front Runner to Performer, and
            Kerala and Tamil Nadu slipped further to the Aspirational group, highlighting emerging
              fiscal pressures.





Fiscal Health Index 2026                                                                                                                 9

Odisha, Gujarat and Maharashtra maintain low debt levels and contain interest burdens,
            supporting fiscal sustainability.

            Conversely, Punjab, Kerala and West Bengal continue to face elevated debt and interest
           commitments, and several mid-tier states show rising leverage, though many remain
             within their existing category bands.



         Highlights: NE/Himalayan States

          The North Eastern (NE) /Himalayan States have been ranked separately from the major
             states and classified into three groups i.e.

              Achievers - Arunachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand

              Performers - Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Sikkim, Tripura

                Aspirational - Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, Nagaland

           Arunachal Pradesh ranks highest, followed by Uttarakhand and Tripura, reflecting
            stronger expenditure quality, revenue capacity and debt management

           Himachal Pradesh and Manipur remain at the bottom due to weak revenues and
             persistent fiscal stress.

          Meghalaya and Assam occupy upper middle positions with mixed indicator
           performance

           Mizoram, Nagaland and Sikkim display uneven performance across different fiscal
             metrics.

             Mizoram has low score under debt sustainability,

               Sikkim scores low on Fiscal Prudence

              Nagaland has lower scores on Quality of Expenditure and Revenue Mobilisation.

           Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya improved through higher capital outlay and
           developmental spending exceeding two-thirds of total expenditure.

             Tripura, Himachal Pradesh and Manipur face crowding-out from large salary and
           pension commitments.

           Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh exhibit relatively stronger own-revenue capacity

             Tripura, Nagaland and Manipur have weaker revenue mobilisation and central transfers
           form over 80% of revenue.

           Arunachal Pradesh maintains lower deficits and occasional surpluses through
             controlled revenue spending, but several states continue to run deficits around 4-5% of





Fiscal Health Index 2026                                                                                                                10

GSDP due to rigid expenditure structures.

          Assam, Tripura and Uttarakhand maintain moderate debt burdens

           Manipur and Himachal Pradesh carry high debt levels of roughly 40-50% of GSDP with
              rising servicing pressures.


      Policy Recommendations for States

       The report suggests several measures fo states to strengthen fiscal sustainability.

           States should improve revenue mobilisation by

              Broadening GST tax base.

               Strengthening state own-tax revenues.

            Rationalise Government Expenditure: States must control committed expenditure such
           as salaries, pensions, and subsidies.

          Improve Quality of Capital Expenditure: States should Enhance productivity of
             infrastructure spending.

          Adopt Medium-Term Fiscal Frameworks: States should implement fiscal plans to
         manage deficits and debt trajectories.

           Strengthen Fiscal Governance: States should improve public financial management
           systems.

           States must manage Debt Risks by

               Tightening control on off-budget borrowings.

               Improving cash and debt management.
